servicesScreen.consequence: Features that depend on this service are affected
servicesScreen.critical: This is a core service: the app may lose its connection to the router

wolScreen.emptyHint: Add a computer's name and MAC address to wake it with one tap. Wake-on-LAN must be enabled in its BIOS and network card.
wolScreen.name: Name

routerEdit.title: Edit Router
routerEdit.passwordHint: Leave empty to keep the current password
routerEdit.deleteConsequence: The app forgets this router's address and saved password; the router itself is untouched

aboutScreen.privacyText: RouteLink collects nothing: no analytics, no ads. The app talks only to the routers you add; passwords stay in the system keychain.
aboutScreen.license: Open source under the MIT License

processesScreen.protected: The kernel and init (PID 1) cannot be stopped
processesScreen.termConsequence: The process ends; services managed by the system usually start again by themselves
processesScreen.killConsequence: The process ends immediately, without saving anything

cronScreen.emptyHint: Tasks run commands as root at set times, e.g. a weekly reboot.
cronScreen.managedHint: Tasks marked App are managed by RouteLink (Wi-Fi schedules) and change on their own pages.

error.fields: Five fields: minute hour day month weekday
error.weekday: Weekday must be 0–7 (0 and 7 are Sunday)

cronScreen.saveConsequence: The command runs as root at the scheduled times
cronScreen.changed: The task list was changed on the router meanwhile; reloaded, please try again

ledsScreen.empty: This router has no LEDs the system can control
ledsScreen.hint: Changes apply right away and stay after a reboot.

systemScreen.passwordHint: The password for LuCI, SSH and this app (account {{user}}).
systemScreen.passwordConsequence: LuCI and SSH need the new password; the app saves it for this router

packagesScreen.typeToSearch: Type at least 2 letters to search the feeds
packagesScreen.noLists: The package lists haven't been downloaded since the router started.
packagesScreen.installConsequence: The router downloads it and what it needs from its package feeds
packagesScreen.removeConsequence: Features that need this package stop working
packagesScreen.cutsOff: The app talks to the router through {{names}}: after removing it, the app (and LuCI) can no longer connect
packagesScreen.failed: The package manager reported an error

unsupported.no-helper: This router has no LuCI package manager (luci-app-package-manager or luci-app-opkg).
unsupported.no-permission: This account isn't allowed to manage packages; sign in as root.

backupScreen.title: Backup and Restore
backupScreen.intro: A backup holds the router's configuration (network, Wi-Fi, firewall, passwords and so on), not the installed packages.
backupScreen.deleteConsequence: Only the file on this phone is deleted; the router is not affected.
backupScreen.sensitive: Backups contain Wi-Fi and admin passwords; take care when sharing them.

restoreRisks.replace: The router's current configuration is replaced by the backup's; changes made since the backup are lost.
restoreRisks.reboot: The router restarts afterwards; every device is offline for 1–2 minutes.
restoreRisks.address: If the backup has another address or admin password, the app has to use those.
restoreRisks.power: Keep the router powered while it restores and restarts.

firmwareScreen.title: Firmware Upgrade
firmwareScreen.checkHint: Asks {{site}} for this router's official firmware.
firmwareScreen.upToDate: This is the latest stable release

unsupported.distribution: This router does not run official OpenWrt or ImmortalWrt; upgrade with a local file.
unsupported.version: Snapshot and test builds have no online upgrade; use a local file.

firmwareScreen.customBuild: This firmware is not the official build (its revision differs); upgrade with a local file.
firmwareScreen.noImage: The official builds have no image for this router; upgrade with a local file.
firmwareScreen.hashMismatch: The downloaded file failed the checksum and was not used. Try again.
firmwareScreen.keepHint: Without it the router comes back with defaults (192.168.1.1, no password).
firmwareScreen.keepUnavailable: Settings can't be kept with this image.
firmwareScreen.forceHint: Flashes an image that failed the checks; the router may not start again.
firmwareScreen.packages: Packages you installed yourself (the RouteLink plugin, SQM, DDNS…) have to be installed again afterwards.

risks.brick: A wrong image or a power cut while flashing can brick the router; recovering then takes a serial console or recovery mode.
risks.time: Flashing and restarting take a few minutes; every device is offline meanwhile.
risks.settings: Without “Keep settings” every setting is lost.
risks.power: Keep the router powered and the app open while it flashes.

risks.erase: Every setting and every package you installed is erased.
risks.address: Afterwards the router is at 192.168.1.1 with no admin password.
risks.wifi: Wi-Fi is usually off afterwards; connect a cable to set the router up again.
risks.power: Keep the router powered while it resets.

backupFirst.title: Back up the current settings first?
backupFirst.message: If something goes wrong, this backup brings them back. It is saved on this phone.

progress.keepPower: Keep the router powered and the app open
progress.waitingDown: Waiting for the router to restart…
progress.waitingUp: Waiting for the router to come back…
progress.resetSameAddress: The router is back at its address and has no admin password now. Set one right away.
progress.resetNewAddress: The router is now at {{address}}. Once the phone is connected to it, switch this router to that address.
progress.timeout: The router did not come back within {{minutes}} minutes
progress.timeoutHint: Check the router's power and lights. Routers that flash slowly may need a little longer.
